Review of 1.24.36's givens (GIVENS, GIVENS_CONTROL, AI_CONTROL's promptOf), draft a43cd2e beside 1.24.35 (8cb3281)
=========================================================================================================

By a reviewer who wrote none of it. Nothing under src/ or tests/ was changed; everything here is under
tests/fixtures/givens_review_1236/.

  node tests/fixtures/givens_review_1236/replay.js [path/to/lantern.inner.html] [--only <id regex>]

  lib.js      loads the draft and 1.24.35 (git show 8cb3281, into the system temp folder) side by side in jsdom
              (load.js, a copy of liftstation_review1_1230's); lib.shown(L, q) is what the model is shown (the given's
              block under "Lantern's tested circuit for this"); lib.make(circuit) a ladder simulator (push buttons,
              overloads, coil and timer contacts, process switches by level/pressure, switches forced by a case)
  judge.js    what each given must be for its question, checked on the circuit Lantern draws from it
  cases_a.js  54 questions each given fits, as people and models phrase them (right fits)
  cases_b.js  79 questions where what is shown must be fitted right (lights, stations, supply, load, cut-out, timer,
              floats) or a near miss caught by a given's words
  cases_c.js  51 near misses that must get no given and 1.24.35's prompt byte for byte
  cases_d.js  12 bench guard cases (prompts, Chat's system prompt full and short, tools, 1221 saved replies, 944 graded
              rows, 66 ideals, the givens copied as they stand)
  cases_e.js  29 module cases (dropped modules, ES5, regex quotes, ASCII, the givens API, drawn as written, correction
              turn, a question of several parts)
  cases_f.js  10 givens changed the way a model changes them for what the question asks beyond them (rule 8)
  run_a43cd2e.txt   the run on the draft: 235 cases, 148 AGREE, 87 DISAGREE (high 47, medium 30, low 10)

Against 1.24.35 itself the same cases give 117 AGREE / 118 DISAGREE (the right fits fail there: no given), so the
cases measure the change.

SUMMARY
-------
What holds: every given, for the questions it was written for, is shown, fitted and right. All 54 right fits agree:
one station and two, run / stopped / both lights, the supply named, the load named; forward/reverse interlocked;
M2 only while M1 runs; the delayed start with its horn sounding only while it times; the compressor's switch
normally closed opening at the cut-out; the fill float normally closed opening as it fills; the sump float normally
open closing as it rises -- each simulated on the circuit Lantern draws. The bench is untouched outside the two
control questions (D, all 12 agree). The modules are droppable, ES5, ASCII, with no quote in a regex literal.

What does not: the fitting and the matching. A given is shown "write it as it stands, changing only what the question
asks" for many questions it does not fit, or fitted wrongly -- and the small models copy what is in front of them.
Where 1.24.35 showed a sump pump "For example", the draft now shows a block to copy: for a two-wire thermostat
question the old example (a switch, two-wire) was nearer right than the three-wire starter now shown.

HIGH (47 cases; grouped by cause)
---------------------------------
H1  Lights (GIVENS_CONTROL lights(); the sump's own light rule).
    Any light word gives a run light; the stopped words are few; "not running" also reads as running; the 50-character
    window crosses into other clauses; in the sump given "alarm" adds a "pump on" light.
    - B-light-trip, B-light-trip-comes-on: an overload trip light asked; shown lamp LT1 M1 "run" green. Expected a trip
      light (lamp LT1 OL1 "overload tripped" amber -- Lantern draws it right, F-starter-overload-light) or none.
    - B-light-none-needed ("no pilot light needed"), B-light-without ("without any indicator lights"): shown a run light.
    - B-light-not-running ("a light that shows the motor is not running"): shown run AND stopped lights.
    - B-light-goes-out ("a pilot light that goes out when the motor runs"): shown a run light, the opposite.
    - B-light-red-stop ("a green run light and a red stop light"), B-light-off-light ("an ON light and an OFF light"),
      B-light-stopped-pilot ("green run and red stopped pilot lights"): the stopped light missing, run only.
    - B-light-window-semicolon ("a run light; the motor is stopped by the stop button or the overload"): an extra
      stopped light.
    - B-light-sump-alarm, B-light-sump-alarm-light ("a sump pump with a high water alarm"): shown
      lamp LT1 M1 "pump on" green as the alarm. Expected an alarm on a second, higher float (the lines
      float FS2 "high level alarm" / lamp LT1 FS2 "high water" red draw right on the given: F-sump-alarm-float) or no light.
H2  Stations (TWO): only "two stations / two locations / local and remote / from two places / sets of buttons".
    - B-sta-two-pb ("two push-button stations"), B-sta-two-startstop ("two start/stop stations"), B-sta-two-buttons-each
      ("two stop buttons and two start buttons"), B-sta-second ("a second start/stop station"), B-sta-both-ends
      ("stations at both ends"): one station shown.
    - B-sta-three ("three start/stop stations"): one station shown. (A model adding a third to the two-station given
      draws right: F-starter-third-station.)
H3  Supply (supply()): the first voltage in the question is taken, whatever it names.
    - B-sup-480-120 ("a 480 V motor starter with a 120 V control transformer"): supply "480 V AC".
    - B-sup-208-24 ("a 208 V motor with 24 V AC control"): supply "208 V AC".
    - B-sup-compressor-230-24 ("a 230 V air compressor ... 24 V AC control"): supply "230 V AC".
H4  Near misses taken by the starter (asks: "motor starter", "start/stop", "<load> starter|contactor"; not too narrow).
    Shown stop PB1 / start PB2 / coil M1 "motor starter" / overload OL1 M1 for:
    - B-nt-two-wire-thermostat, B-nt-fan-thermostat, B-nt-two-wire-toggle (two-wire control: no start, no seal-in),
    - B-nt-hoa (hand-off-auto), B-nt-vfd (a drive's run command), B-nt-y-delta ("Y-delta"), B-nt-star-slash-delta
      ("star/delta"), B-nt-2-speed ("2-speed": only "two-speed" is excluded), B-nt-dual-speed, B-nt-autotransformer,
      B-nt-part-winding.
H5  Sequence matched by the bare word "sequence"; motors counted as two.
    - B-sq-sequence-of-operation ("a motor starter and explain its sequence of operation"), B-sq-number-rungs
      ("number the rungs in sequence"): the two-motor sequence given for one motor.
    - B-sq-three-conveyors ("three conveyors that start in sequence"): two motors shown.
H6  Delayed start.
    - B-dl-off-delay-fan ("a fan keeps running 5 minutes after the burner shuts off, using a time delay relay"),
      B-dl-off-delay-light ("turns off a light 30 seconds after the push button is released"): off-delays shown the
      on-delay motor given ("time delay relay" alone fits it).
    - B-dl-two-motors ("motor 2 starts 10 seconds after motor 1"): a one-motor given.
    - B-dl-ondelay-light (an on-delay timer lighting a lamp from a switch): push buttons, a starter, an overload.
    - B-dl-overload-restart: a defect in the given itself. OL1 is only in M1's rung; CR1 stays sealed in and TR1 timed
      out, so when OL1 is reset M1 restarts at once, with nobody pressing start and no warning -- the pre-start
      warning the given is for is skipped (NEC 430.43's concern; a three-wire circuit's point). The mend is one line:
      overload OL1 M1 CR1  -- F-delayed-overload-mend: drawn clean, stays stopped after the reset, warns on the next start.
H7  Compressor: B-cp-low-pressure-refrig ("a refrigeration compressor with a low pressure switch that cuts out at
    20 psi"): shown the air compressor's  pressure PS1 M1 nc "cut-out 20 psi"  under "normally closed, it opens as the
    pressure rises to the cut-out" -- a low-pressure cut-out opens as the pressure FALLS (drawn normally open, held
    closed by pressure). The direction the task names.
H8  Fill: the not-words are whole words, so "drains", "empties", "draining" pass.
    - B-fl-fill-then-drain ("fills a tank and then drains it"), B-fl-fill-and-empty ("a pump that fills a tank and a
      pump that empties it"): the one-pump fill given.
    - B-fl-two-floats ("fills a tank with a high and a low float"): one float shown.
H9  Sump: B-sp-refrigeration-pumpdown ("a refrigeration pump-down cycle"), B-sp-pumpdown-solenoid ("a pump down system
    with a liquid line solenoid and a low pressure control"): the sump pump on a float. B-sp-on-off-floats ("on and off
    floats"): one float shown (the two floats a model would add draw right and hold in: F-sump-on-off-floats).

MEDIUM (30)
-----------
- Lights: B-light-power (a power-on light shown as a run light), B-light-light-duty ("light-duty conveyor" -> a run
  light), B-light-window-is-off ("a pilot light, and make sure the motor is off when the overload trips" -> a stopped
  light instead of the run light), B-light-fault-reversing (a fault light -> forward and reverse lights).
- Supply: B-sup-460-motor (460V motor -> supply "460 V AC" shown as the control's); B-sup-24vdc-joined ("24VDC" -> no
  supply, though the module's own comment says it reads 24VDC), B-sup-24vac-joined ("24 VAC"), B-sup-120vac-joined
  ("120 VAC"): no supply.
- Load: B-load-press-verb ("press start to run" -> coil M1 "press starter"), B-load-fan-pumphouse ("a fan in the pump
  house" -> "pump starter": LOADS is searched in list order, not question order), B-load-seq-crusher ("the conveyor must
  start after the crusher" -> "conveyor 1" / "conveyor 2"), B-load-seq-fan-pump ("the pump can only run when the
  cooling fan is running" -> "pump 1" / "pump 2").
- Compressor: B-cp-30-above ("the cut-out is 30 psi above the cut-in of 90 psi" -> "cut-out 30 psi").
- Timer: B-dl-float-starts (a float-started delay -> push buttons), B-dl-two-times ("a 5 second warning horn, then the
  conveyor starts 20 seconds after" -> timer "5 s").
- Fill: B-fl-solenoid-valve (a solenoid valve filling -> pump starter and overload), B-fl-alarm-only (a high level
  alarm on a tank filling line -> the fill pump given).
- Starter near misses: B-nt-soft-starter, B-nt-inch, B-nt-lighting-contactor, B-nt-latch-light, B-nt-solenoid-seal,
  B-nt-heater-contactor (motor starter with an overload for loads with no motor), B-nt-programmable-relay,
  B-nt-warning-horn (a pre-start warning horn -> the plain starter).
- C-jogging-reversing ("forward/reverse jogging") -> the reversing given (its not has no jog).
- C-motor-no-control ("What size wire do I need for a 5 HP motor starter?"), C-explain-3wire ("Explain how a
  three-wire start/stop circuit works"): not drawings, shown a block "to write as it stands". 1.24.35 offered MAKE
  CONTROL here too (the words wire / circuit), but as an example.
- E-api-bad-user-given: Lantern.givens.add accepts any truthy asks; with asks a string, match() calls g.asks.test and
  act.prompt AND Chat's system prompt throw for every control question. A user's given (rule 8) can break Chat.
- F-fill-two-floats: pre-existing, found through the givens: a fill pump on two floats cannot be drawn with its hold-in
  (AI_CONTROL holds in an emptying pump's floats only), so the second float B-fl-two-floats asks for cannot be added
  to the fill given right: rising 5/15/25 then falling 15/5 the pump is on, off, off, off, on (short-cycles at FS1).

LOW (10)
--------
- B-sta-workstations ("a conveyor that carries parts between two stations" -> two push-button stations).
- B-sup-24v-no-kind ("24 V" -> "24 V DC"; 24 V control is as often AC).
- B-load-saw-verb ("as I saw in the manual" -> coil M1 "saw starter").
- B-cp-low-oil (a low oil pressure switch asked; one pressure switch shown).
- B-nt-estop (an e-stop asked; the fitted given has none, and the model is told to write it as it stands; an added
  "estop ES1" draws right: F-starter-estop).
- E-isolation-test-lists: tests/ai_isolation.js does not list GIVENS or GIVENS_CONTROL, so the suite does not prove
  them droppable on each run (I proved it by hand: E-drop-*; ai_isolation.js itself passes, 169 modules).
- E-api-kept: rule 8's "kept as the user's own given" is not there: add() keeps a given in memory, nothing saves or
  loads one, and nothing in Chat or an app calls add.
- E-as-written-reversing: every reversing drawing carries Lantern's note "PB1 stops everything: it is drawn in L1 ahead
  of every rung (name a coil to stop just one: stop PB1 M1)" -- from the given's own "stop PB1".
  E-as-written-sequence: "PB1 is drawn in M1 and M2's rungs: one contact of it in each" -- from "stop PB1 M1 M2".
  A tested given should draw with no correction under it.
- E-reversing-one-overload-twice: "overload OL1 M1 M2" draws OL1's contact in both rungs; NEMA/JIC reversing diagrams
  draw the one overload contact once, in the common line.

AGREE (148) -- what was checked and holds
------------------------------------------
- A (54/54): every given shown and right for the phrasings it fits, simulated on Lantern's drawing (see SUMMARY).
- C (48/51): jog, two-speed, star-delta, wye-delta, PLC programs (start/stop, forward/reverse, sequence, compressor),
  duplex lift stations and sump pumps, two sump pumps, two/duplex/alternating compressors, pneumatic, hydraulic,
  transistor, 555, Arduino, light switches, three-way, doorbell, water heater, motor with a thermostat (no "starter"
  in it), fill and drain with two pumps, a pump that fills and a valve that drains, drum switch, door light relay,
  limit switch, VFD wiring, HOA pump on a float, boiler, transfer switch, traffic lights, flasher, well pump on a
  pressure switch, refrigeration high/low switches, hoist up/down, garage door, elevator, "why does a seal-in...",
  overload sizing: no given, and the prompt byte-identical to 1.24.35's.
- D (12/12): only make-control and make-control-b get a given; act.prompt for every other question of both bench sets
  byte-identical; Chat's system prompt (CHAT.buildSystem) byte-identical in full and in short mode (and different for
  the two control questions); act.relevant identical; the two control prompts keep every line before the example
  ("For example:" taken off) and end with the one given block; 1221 saved replies from 944 rows in
  tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json build as on 1.24.35 (ok, kind, readAs, problems, summary, circuit); 944 rows graded
  as on 1.24.35; 66 ideals grade as on 1.24.35 and both control ideals pass; both givens pass their bench questions
  copied as they stand, after a sentence, under the given's own line, in a code fence and without END; neither given
  is its bench ideal word for word.
- E (23/29): without GIVENS_CONTROL, without GIVENS, without both: boots with no error, the prompt is 1.24.35's, every
  bench prompt and system prompt builds, make-control's ideal passes; without AI_CONTROL: boots, givens there, nothing
  throws. GIVENS, GIVENS_CONTROL and AI_CONTROL parse as ES5; no quote in a regex literal; ASCII only; Depends headers
  right. A user's given (well-formed) is shown and replaced by a second add; a given whose block throws or is empty
  leaves the prompt as before. The correction turn is as 1.24.35's. In a question of several parts the given is fitted
  to the control part. What a given is, is said above its block; nothing stands after it but another tool's own
  instructions.
- F (9/10): the givens are a sound base for the changes a question asks beyond them: an e-stop, a stopped light, a
  third station, an overload trip light, end-of-travel limits on forward/reverse, a sump's alarm float, a sump's on and
  off floats (held in, no short-cycling), the delayed start's overload mend, a compressor with start/stop -- each drawn
  clean and right in simulation.

PRE-EXISTING (not the change; seen on the way)
----------------------------------------------
- "Draw a reverse and forward motor control circuit..." is split by AI_PARTS into "Draw a reverse" (MAKE DRAWING) and
  the rest, on 1.24.35 too.
- "Draw a delayed start circuit for a conveyor...", "Draw a tank filling pump control with a float", "Draw a pump-down
  control for a pit with a float switch", "Draw a sequence control: pump 2 can't start until pump 1 runs" never reach
  the control prompt (AI_CONTROL.asks is false), so no given either.
- Fill phrasings the fill given misses (no harm, a miss): "keeps the tank full", "fill a water trough", "fills a
  storage tank".

COULD NOT RUN
-------------
- No model at all: not the 0.8B, 2B or 4B (the bench workflow runs on a push; nothing was pushed) and not the 35B (no
  laptop). Whether a small model copies these givens better or worse than the old example is untested; every case
  here judges what the model is SHOWN and what Lantern draws from the given as shown.
- No drawing was rendered in Chromium (the change does not touch DRAW_LADDER; the circuits were read from the plan and
  simulated, not looked at).
- npm test (the whole suite) was not run. Run: tests/givens_1236.js (22 pass), tests/control.js (41 pass),
  tests/float_switch_1235.js (10 pass), tests/ai_isolation.js (169 modules isolated).
- The NEC/NFPA references are from knowledge, not opened pages; the circuit judgments rest on the simulation and
  ordinary NEMA/JIC ladder practice.
